modules.title: Comparative Public Policy And Development
modules.summary: Delve into the dynamic world of comparative public policy and development. This course equips you to dissect policy decisions across diverse contexts, from grassroots advocacy to high-level international negotiations. You'll explore the unseen forces – media narratives, special interest pressures, and political calculations – that shape policy agendas. Through critical analysis of decision-making models and implementation challenges, you'll gain the expertise to navigate the complex interplay between policy, politics, and development on a global scale.

outcomes: Evaluate the effectiveness of public policies using various methods, including cost-benefit analysis, outcome evaluation, and process evaluation.
Understand and analyse the informal processes and actors that influence public policy-making.
Analyse the role of mass media in shaping public opinion and influencing policy-making.
Analyze the rhetoric and statements of political leaders and assess their impact on public policy.
Understand the role of special interest groups in shaping public policy and analyze how these groups exert influence.
Understand and apply different models of decision-making, including the rational model, incremental model, bounded rationality model, and consensus-building models.
Understand the relationship between politics and administration in shaping development, and analyze the ways in which this relationship affects the implementation of public policy.
